message.reasoning_content: The kernel: row-sum of (64,128) with values like ±w (up to 32M) plus small 0.25–0.75. Sequential float32 summation: large values cancel (w and -w), so intermediate magnitudes huge; small terms get absorbed catastrophically. w*1048576 up to ~3.36e7, small values 0.25–0.75 → ulp at 3e7 is 2. Sequential float32 accumulation could lose all small terms; error ~ sum of 64 small values up to ~32 per row, vs reference norm... reference = sum of small values (w cancels -w exactly in real arithmetic), so reference per row up to ~32, ‖ref‖₂ maybe ~15. Error would be significant. But depends on permutation order — partial sums of w/-w can be huge mid-sum. Likely E > 0.1 → reject. Let's record claim and run probe.
